label: Latency alert on orders-api
description: Order creation p95 6.4s with 503s and Postgres refusing connections.

evidence.title: orders-api: order creation latency 6.4s p95 with 503s
evidence.detail: POST /v2/orders is timing out: p95 6.4s (baseline 180ms), 503 responses and 'too many clients already' errors from Postgres. Monitor: orders_api.dependency_timeouts{service=orders-api}.

evidence.title: orders-api v4.9.2 deployed 40 minutes before the alert
evidence.detail: Order export feature: analytics joins enabled by default on the order search path. Deployed by @p.novak, 18 files changed, medium risk.

evidence.title: orders-api degraded; postgres-orders unhealthy
evidence.detail: orders-api status=degraded. postgres-orders status=unhealthy: 200/200 connections, 'too many clients already', slow query on order_items. redis-cache healthy at 41/100 clients.

hint: Which pool is actually saturated? Check the database before assuming the cache.

label: Database pool saturation
description: The Postgres pool is full and one query is holding connections for 4.2 seconds.

evidence.title: DB pool saturated: acquired 200/200, queued 143, wait p95 4180ms
evidence.detail: orders-api has 200 acquired connections and 143 requests queued. Postgres reports max_connections reached; 9 sessions are waiting on Lock.

evidence.title: Slow query: orders_search_by_customer avg 4.2s (seq scan on order_items)
evidence.detail: pg_stat_statements top total_time = SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN order_items ... WHERE o.customer_id = $1, avg 4210ms. EXPLAIN shows a seq scan; order_items was last analyzed 9 days ago.

evidence.title: redis-cache healthy: 41/100 clients, 1.1ms p95, zero cache failures
evidence.detail: orders-api logged no cache acquisition failures for this incident window. The cache is not involved.

hint: The cache is healthy. The historical Redis playbook is contradicted by current evidence - say so explicitly instead of reusing it.

label: Restart mitigation applied
description: Reachable only by executing the restart action. No improvement at all.

evidence.title: After rolling restart: acquired 200/200 again within 25s, no change in failure rate
evidence.detail: New workers re-established 200 connections onto the same 4.2s query. Postgres refused the remaining slots; failure rate unchanged at 18.4%.

hint: The mitigation had no effect because the constraint is the query, not the process.

label: Service recovered
description: Index added and analytics join disabled, service stable.

evidence.title: Resolved: query p95 190ms, pool 61/200, 5xx 0.3%
evidence.detail: orders_search_by_customer p95 190ms after CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_order_items_customer plus ANALYZE. Connection pool stable at 61/200.

hint: Stable. The lesson to retain: the recalled Redis precedent was contradicted, and the database pool was the real constraint.
